facts.raw_span: A woman in her 40s presented with a 10-year history of progressive skin thickening and subcutaneous enlargement of the right side of her nose and right cheek
she had undergone nondiagnostic skin biopsies
she underwent a septorhinoplasty 6 months prior due to collapse of her right nasal ala
significant submucosal tissue was noted and removed from the right nasal cavity
she initially improved but noticed enlargement of soft tissue with thickening of the overlying skin on her right cheek and right side of her nose several months later
slightly hyperplastic soft tissue with dilated patulous follicles involving the right medial malar cheek and right nasal ala in addition to deviation of the nasal tip
initial septorhinoplasty specimens showed fibroadipose tissue and vascular proliferation
initial skin biopsy was interpreted as sebaceous hyperplasia
subcutaneous-based proliferation of spindle cells with varying density
thickened and fragmented collagen bundles
mature adipocytes extending into skeletal tissue
spindle cells had bland cytomorphology with tapered nuclei and ill-defined cytoplasm
no cellular pleomorphism observed

concepts.why: The presence of fibroadipose tissue, vascular proliferation, and thickened collagen bundles supports this diagnosis.
The subcutaneous-based proliferation of spindle cells, mature adipocytes extending into skeletal tissue, and bland cytomorphology of spindle cells support this diagnosis.
The initial skin biopsy interpreted as sebaceous hyperplasia and the presence of dilated patulous follicles support this diagnosis.

rationales.F01: Progressive skin thickening and subcutaneous enlargement suggests a possible lipomatous or fibrolipomatous process.
rationales.F04: Removal of significant submucosal tissue from the right nasal cavity may indicate a process involving the nasal cavity.
rationales.F06: Slightly hyperplastic soft tissue with dilated patulous follicles involving the right medial malar cheek and right nasal ala suggests a possible lipomatous or fibrolipomatous process.
rationales.F07: Fibroadipose tissue and vascular proliferation in the initial septorhinoplasty specimens suggest a possible lipomatous or fibrolipomatous process.
rationales.F09: Subcutaneous-based proliferation of spindle cells with varying density is highly suggestive of a spindle cell lipoma or fibrolipomatous hamartoma.
rationales.F10: Thickened and fragmented collagen bundles suggest a possible fibromatous or fibrolipomatous process.
rationales.F11: Mature adipocytes extending into skeletal tissue is highly suggestive of a lipomatous or fibrolipomatous process.
rationales.F12: Spindle cells with bland cytomorphology and tapered nuclei are highly suggestive of a spindle cell lipoma or fibrolipomatous hamartoma.
